answer: Neighborhood Beacon Reach** Each agent periodically emits a beacon recording its verified neighbor set; an identity counts as valid only if its reachable neighborhood exceeds a threshold and its neighbors' neighborhoods overlap (clustering). Isolated identities form an island with low reach and are ignored for routing and reward. An attacker must build genuine, mutually overlapping links across many honest peers—each fake identity needs sustained traffic and real counterparts, so cost scales with edge count, not registration.
